speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Transport (a) how many e-bike models have been approved to date and of these how many are additional new models that have been approved since January 2023; (b) in the past three years, how many e-bikes have been registered; (c) how many e-bikes are detected to be illegal; (d) how many riders are caught for not riding at approved places; and (e) how many accidents have been recorded.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Speaker, I thank the Senior Parliamentary Secretary for the comprehensive reply.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: With the Certificates of Entitlement (COEs) rising month after month and breaking records, more Singaporeans, understandably, will turn to e-bikes for their mobility solutions.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: So, would the Ministry of Transport (MOT) consider working with the e-bike suppliers to broaden the models available for Singaporeans to choose?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Two, what are MOT's plans to discourage and deter more illegal e-bikes to be used on the road?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: There are many e-bike fire incidents in different parts of Singapore, including in the Nanyang area.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Thirdly, what are MOT's plans to build more pathways and cycling paths to enable e-bike riders to ride safely on the pavement, rather than on the road?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: We understand that MOT has announced some plans to build cycling paths, but we are asking MOT whether it can intensify and accelerate the progress.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In fact, the numbers have been increasing, especially in recent years.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As the demand grows, the retailers would be incentivised to import more models – models that are certified to be safe for use on paths and roads.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As to ensuring that riders ride safely and properly on approved paths, public education and enforcement are carried out.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: For the offences that have been detected, the culprits were fined accordingly.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We hope this will give the signal to riders to understand the law, abide by the law and, most importantly, look out for other users, whether on the path or on the road.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: PABs are allowed on the roads, as well as on cycling paths.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Yes, some riders would find it safer to be on cycling paths.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: That is why we are aggressively rolling out the islandwide cycling network.
